```{python}
#| echo: false
from _common import *
import dask
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

BRAN2023, the Bluelink ocean reanalysis (CSIRO and the Bureau of
Meteorology), is daily, 0.1 degree, 51 levels, from 1993: hundreds of
terabytes of netCDF on NCI's THREDDS server. kerchunk references in
Parquet describe every chunk of every file, and GDAL's Zarr driver
reads them as one store. See [Byte-reference stores](../guide/byte-refs.qmd)
for what such a reference table holds.

THREDDS limits aggressive parallel reads. Eight threads is a safe cap:

```{python}
dask.config.set(scheduler="threads", num_workers=8)
```

## A pinned reference store

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
status_callout("bran-virtualized-pinned")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
dsn = ('ZARR:"/vsicurl/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdsumner/virtualized/'
       'd0b9c23317d2de07c3851eb9dfc968be1761d5b8/zarr/ocean_temp.zarr"')
if live("bran-virtualized-pinned"):
    bran = xr.open_dataset(dsn, engine="gdalxarray", drop_variables=["Time_bnds"])
    print(bran)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
assert dsn == store("bran-virtualized-pinned")["dsn"]
```

`Time` comes through as numbers here: the references carry the values
and units of the source, and decoding them is a one-liner if they are
not decoded already. One day's surface temperature over the Tasman
Sea, chunked so dask reads the few chunks in parallel:

```{python}
#| error: true
#| fig-cap: "BRAN2023 surface temperature, first day of the store, read through kerchunk references from THREDDS."
if live("bran-virtualized-pinned"):
    surf = (bran["temp"].isel(Time=0, st_ocean=0)
            .sel(yt_ocean=slice(-48, -25), xt_ocean=slice(145, 170))
            .chunk({"yt_ocean": 300, "xt_ocean": 300}).load())
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
    surf.plot(ax=ax, cmap="RdYlBu_r")
    ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.radians(-36)))
    plt.show()
```

## Yearly reference stores on Pawsey

The same references, one store per variable per year, hosted on
Pawsey's object store and opened through a `vrt://` wrapper:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
status_callout("bran-pawsey-2023")
```

```{python}
#| error: true
dsn = "vrt:///vsicurl/https://projects.pawsey.org.au/aad-index/vzarr/ocean_temp_2023.parq"
if live("bran-pawsey-2023"):
    b23 = xr.open_dataset(dsn, engine="gdalxarray",
                          drop_variables=["Time_bnds", "DT", "average_DT", "average_T1", "average_T2"])
    print(dict(b23.sizes))
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
assert dsn == store("bran-pawsey-2023")["dsn"]
```
